paper_title: How to Generate Popular Post Headlines on Social Media
caption: The average similarities between the headlines from different seasons
model_annotation: This line plot illustrates the average similarity of headlines across different seasonal intervals, measured in days. The x-axis, labeled “Δ Days,” is categorical and divided into five bins: (0,90], (90,180], (180,270], (270,360], and (360,450], representing time periods in days. The y-axis, labeled “Avg. similarity (10e-2),” is linear and scaled from 1.70 to 1.85, indicating similarity values multiplied by 10 to the power of -2. A single light blue dashed line with circular markers connects the data points for each interval, showing a general downward trend. The similarity begins at approximately 1.845 for the first interval (0–90 days), decreases to about 1.80 for the second (90–180 days), then drops further to around 1.73 for the third (180–270 days), rises slightly to about 1.745 for the fourth (270–360 days), and finally declines to approximately 1.695 for the final interval (360–450 days).
